newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to stress on prudent spending in Budget.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to stress on prudent spending in Budget.

text.p: Malaysia's 1998 Budget policy will stress on prudent spending to avoid unnecessary spending and wastage, acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday.
Speaking at a budget dialogue session, he said the country needed to strengthen its economic structure in order to continue achieving quality growth.

Government expenditure must be according to allocation and additional expenditure outside the allocated sum would not be allowed unless approved by federal agencies for urgent cases of health, education and rural development programmes, said Anwar.

The country's existing strong financial standing ought to be closely nurtured by regulatory authorities, and banks should have prudent internal management, said Anwar, also Malaysia's finance minister.

"This is to prevent Malaysia from being affected by (the) financial crisis which had affected a few other countries recently as a result of non-performing loans in view of the over-exposure of their banking systems to the property sector and the poor quality of loans," he said.
The 1998 Budget will be unveiled in October.
